title: FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit — Application Underwriting and Opening Terms
content:
**Clause 1 — Tier placement.** An applicant is approved into the highest tier whose credit score, debt-to-income and income requirements they meet, with a limit inside that tier's limit range set by underwriting; an applicant who meets no tier is declined.

**Clause 2 — Combined unsecured exposure.** A FlexLine is assessed together with the customer's Larkspur Personal Loans: the new credit limit plus the unpaid principal of the customer's active personal loans may not exceed 75000.00 USD, and a customer with a personal loan in charged-off status or more than 30 days past due is declined. The limit is reduced to fit the combined cap and the application is declined if the reduced limit is below the tier's minimum. These facts are taken from Larkspur's own records of the customer's personal loans (their status, unpaid principal and next due date), checked before the line is opened.

**Clause 3 — Opening APR.** The APR at opening is the Prime Rate plus the tier margin, not below the tier floor and not above the APR cap. The Prime Rate used is the index named in the product's rate schedule.

**Clause 4 — Draw period.** The draw period ends the tier's draw-period months, counted as whole calendar months after the open date (the last day of that month when the day does not exist).

The tier figures these clauses read — credit score, debt-to-income and income requirements, limit ranges, margins, floors and draw periods — are the tier figures of FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical inputs)

**Combined cap, reduced limit.** Underwriting sets a 12000.00 USD limit for an applicant placed in FlexLine Preferred, whose active personal loans carry 66000.00 USD of unpaid principal. The sum, 78000.00 USD, is above 75000.00 USD, so the limit is reduced to 9000.00 USD, which fits the cap; 9000.00 USD is not below FlexLine Preferred's lowest limit of 7500 USD, so the line opens at 9000.00 USD.

**Combined cap, declined.** With 70000.00 USD of unpaid principal instead, the limit would have to fall to 5000.00 USD, which is below 7500 USD, so the application is declined.

**Personal loan status.** An applicant whose personal loan is 31 days past due is declined; one whose loan is exactly 30 days past due is not declined on that ground, since the clause turns on more than 30 days.

**Draw-period end at month end.** For a line opened on 29 February of a leap year with a 36-month draw period, the matching day does not exist 36 months later, so the draw period ends on 28 February of that year.
